body:
T110 shipped the listing door with a bounded page and a yield between resolutions. Both are containments, not fixes. The cost is still linear in the whole ground, three times over.

MEASURED on T110's repair branch (memory backend, 2026-08-12):

| ground | membership eval | per entity | list(limit 25) | list(limit 100) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2k deltas / 200 entities | 150ms | 120ms | 3.2s | 13.1s |
| 10k deltas / 500 entities | 874ms | 655ms | 17.6s | 71.2s |

Three separate costs, and they want three different remedies.

1. THE MEMBERSHIP EVALUATION IS NOT MAINTAINED. `select` re-runs over the whole ground on every page. Myk's design premise was that a container gives a pre-filtered list that follows the ground live; today the container gives the QUERY, and the query is evaluated per read. An incrementally maintained membership is what the design assumed.

2. THE PROJECTION IS QUADRATIC ON A CURSOR WALK. Every page projects every member delta into entity ids, sorts the whole id set, and only then applies `after` and `limit`. Walking N entities at any page size costs O(N) pages x O(N) ids. A cursor that could seek would make the walk linear.

3. A COLD RESOLUTION IS O(ground). `resolvedNode` is the point door's own cost, not the listing's invention — but the listing multiplies it by the page size. Warm materializations are the read side's existing affordance and nothing wires them to this door.

H8 is the hazard on all three: none of them returns a WRONG answer, which is why they keep passing review. The bound grows monotonically with the store.

WHAT THE CAP COSTS TODAY: LISTING_MAX_LIMIT is 25 and LISTING_DEFAULT_LIMIT is 10. Those literals are pinned by test/gateway/listing.test.ts and they are a measurement, not a preference — raising either without re-measuring re-opens the stall T110's P5 caught (the first cap of 500 bought one authed request ~330 seconds of blocked event loop at a 10k ground).

DONE WHEN: a page's cost is independent of the store's size for costs 1 and 2, and the cap can rise on evidence rather than on hope.
title: The listing door is O(ground) per entity — warm the resolution, maintain the candidate set
